angles.drive: You calm people down without trying to. Taking in someone's worry costs you less than watching them carry it, so you take it in and give back something steadier. Let a little of it out somewhere, because calm you only absorb runs dry.
angles.cost_self: Being the calm one is a job you never put down. You take in other people's upset and level it, while yours waits for a quiet that never comes. Let someone steady you for once, because your own upset is the one left unsettled.
angles.cost_others: When someone close to you is upset, you become the calm for both. Being needed suits you more than being known, and your own trouble never shows. Let them see you shaken sometimes, because calm with nothing behind it keeps people at a distance.

angles.drive: You soak things up rather than study them. It settles into you from whatever is nearby, so you know a thing long before you can pass a test on it. Trust it anyway, since the proof shows up later than the understanding.
angles.cost_self: Soaking it up is how learning stays with you. Sitting with it until it is yours comes easier than proving it on paper, and the proof is the part you skip. Get the paper anyway, because the chances asking for it close without you.
angles.cost_others: You soak up what someone says before deciding whether you agree. Taking it in is easier for you than pushing back, so your disagreement stays where it helps no one. Say it anyway, because you help more with an honest no than a kind yes.

angles.drive: Being patient comes easily to you. Letting a thing come in its own time feels more honest than forcing it, and you can wait on a question for months. Keep your pace, because the price is only the chance that needed a push.
angles.cost_self: Being patient also means you never have to ask. Waiting for a thing to come to you feels easier than reaching, so the wanting stays quiet until the chance passes. Say it once, because what you never asked for is what you gave up unnoticed.
angles.cost_others: You wait for a person to be ready rather than hurry them toward it. Not hurrying feels like respect, and you let someone stay stuck longer than kindness needed. Push sometimes, because being patient is also the hand you kept back.

angles.drive: You let things drift rather than decide them, and you call it patience. There is more Water in you than you turn into motion, so choosing costs more than going along. Remember that when you drift you are choosing too, just not the outcome.
angles.cost_self: Drifting spares you a wrong turn. A decision avoided feels like a risk avoided, and you renew the lease rather than ask what you want next. You pay for each drifted chance in years, and that is worth keeping in mind.
angles.cost_others: Whatever you let drift, you leave to someone else. Being carried feels easier than steering, and you let the people close to you make the calls you never did. It helps to remember that you hand them the weight of every call you dodge.

angles.drive: You stay where it is safe long after outgrowing it. Shelter is the thing you trust most, so you pick the known ahead of the better whenever the two come apart. Remember that you keep the shelter even after you walk out of it.
angles.cost_self: Staying in is how you avoid being tested. Not being ready feels more honest than being ready, and you stay long past the day leaving was open to you. Remember that you give up the very chances the shelter was for by never stepping out.
angles.cost_others: Staying sheltered keeps you home while others go out. You pick being safe ahead of being there, and watch the invitations thin out instead of going. Remember that you offer those you love your safety in place of your company.

angles.drive: You over-protect the people you love from what they could survive. Watching someone struggle hurts you more than doing it for them, so the help comes before the asking. Keep in mind how completely you can protect someone, until not even the lesson reaches them.
angles.cost_self: Over-protecting the ones you love never rests. Taking the hit for someone is easier for you than watching them take it, so you carry what was never yours. Bear in mind what you pay in rest for every hit you absorb for another person.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone you love is about to struggle, you over-protect and step in first. Sparing them the hard part feels like love, and you choose their comfort rather than their growing. Remember that you take from them the one lesson that would have stuck.

angles.drive: You restore people by being the place where nothing is asked of them. The advice waits until requested, the clock stays out of it, and the visit can be silent without being strange. Their levels rise in your company because your company charges nothing. The mechanism is shelter.
angles.cost_self: Your brother let himself in with the spare key, sat in your kitchen for two hours, and said almost nothing. You read nearby and refilled his glass once. He left standing straighter. The visit will never be mentioned, which is exactly why it worked.
angles.cost_others: People route their worst weeks through your place: the call made from your driveway before going home, the couch that has caught every crisis since 2015. Nobody plans it out loud. The harbor is simply known, the way water is known to be downhill.

angles.drive: Your calm is deep water, not thin ice. Provocations sink into it and are absorbed, deadlines land softly on it, and chaos arrives to find no surface tension to grab. It is not detachment. Everything registers. It just registers into stillness instead of splash.
angles.cost_self: The kitchen caught fire, briefly, at the family gathering, and your voice never left its usual register: pan lid, baking soda, window, done. The story afterward was all about the flames. You remember it as a Tuesday.
angles.cost_others: Storms wear themselves out on you without your doing anything. The furious arrive, talk, slow down, and leave merely tired, their weather absorbed into something deeper than it was. You never argue anyone calm. They pour it in, and the water takes it.

angles.drive: You take things in fully before responding, which has become rare enough to feel like a gift. The half-formed idea, the clumsy confession, the criticism with truth in it: all get received whole, unjudged on arrival, given somewhere calm to finish becoming what they meant.
angles.cost_self: Your friend rehearsed the coming-out speech for weeks, and your entire response was to refill their glass and ask how long they had known. The speech had prepared for weather. Your table offered none, and the rest of the evening was just dinner, which was everything.
angles.cost_others: People tell you things they have told no one, over ordinary kitchen tables, at ordinary volumes, startled to hear themselves. The secret is that nothing bounces off you. Whatever arrives is received at depth, held without ripples, and everyone somehow knows this before they test it.

angles.drive: The current decides, and you call it flexibility. The job found you, the apartment happened, the relationship drifted into being and later drifted elsewhere. Choosing feels like swimming upstream, so you float, and your life is largely the record of where the water went.
angles.cost_self: The promotion required a one-paragraph application, and the deadline passed while the paragraph existed fully formed in your head. Someone else applied and got it. You felt something for a week, then adjusted, as you always adjust. Adjustment is the one thing you never postpone.
angles.cost_others: The people who love you have learned that wanting things for you is a solo activity. They set up the interview, the introduction, the viewing, and watch the opening drift past unclaimed. You thank them warmly. The warmth is real. So is the drift, every time.

angles.drive: You absorbed everyone’s everything for years, and the saturation is starting to show. Other people’s moods soak into you and stay, their crises sit in your tissue, and lately your own feelings need a day to surface through the accumulated weather of everybody else’s.
angles.cost_self: After your friend’s two-hour download of her divorce, she felt wonderful and you slept badly, again, carrying cargo that was never yours to store. You woke tired in a specific way that has become your baseline. Somewhere under all of it, presumably, your own mood waits.
angles.cost_others: People treat you as infinite absorbency and you have never corrected the impression. The tears land on you at every gathering, and nobody asks what you do with the volume. Loved ones have started noticing the water line. You change the subject, which is itself the water line.

angles.drive: Comfort has slowly sealed you in. The soft routine, the safe circle, the familiar cup in the familiar chair: each layer was reasonable, and together they have become a membrane between you and anything with weather in it. Inside is warm. Inside is also where everything now has to happen.
angles.cost_self: The invitation to teach abroad, the one that would have thrilled you at thirty, got a full day of consideration and a gentle no. The reasons were practical and real and also, you noticed at two in the morning, identical to last year’s reasons, and the year before’s.
angles.cost_others: Friends have stopped proposing the ambitious version of anything to you, pre-shrinking plans to fit what you will accept: nearer, shorter, softer. The cocoon is comfortable and communal now. Everyone helps maintain it, and everyone, including you, wonders occasionally what it was for.
